metadata.case_name: JOAN CAROL BOIVIN v. WONG KING YIN AND YANWIDE INTERNATIONAL LIMITED

injuries.description: severe "whiplash injury" to her cervical spine
source: severe "whiplash injury" to her cervical spine
Dr Hsu further assessed that, assuming her condition did not improve, the plaintiff's permanent incapacity from the orthopaedic injury is 5% of the whole person.
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain, stiffness or tenderness only

source: Evidence given by Dr Singer, the plaintiff's psychiatrist, suggests that the plaintiff is suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder
this is agreed to by the doctors, both for the plaintiff and the defendants.

injuries.description: depressive disorder or an adjustment disorder with depressive moods
source: Evidence given by Dr Singer, the plaintiff's psychiatrist, suggests that the plaintiff is suffering from ... depressive disorder.
the difference between Dr Singer and Dr Chung is really one of degree.
I find that the plaintiff did, for a period of time after the accident, feel very depressed.
That she still suffers from some depression is accepted by Dr Chung who states that in his opinion she would require some 10 sessions of psychological treatment.

manifestations.description: numbness in the 4th and 5th fingers of her left hand
pain radiating down her left leg from her buttock region
reduced ability to carry out work as a professional photographer

losses.description: Pain has prevented her from carrying out her work as a professional photographer as effectively and affected the business and growth of Goldphoto
Pain has interfered with her social and personal life and she is more withdrawn socially
